messages:
Alex: ran a quick matrix: FP8 vs INT8 vs 4-bit on the a100-dedicated pool. seeing a 15-35% token latency regression for 4-bit at sequence lengths >1024 when KV cache warms up. posting the profiler dump below.

Alex: ```
profile: run_id=2026-02-18T09:12Z
seq_len=128/512/1024
batch=8
kernels: int8_kv_fused: 160us/token, fp8_kv_fused: 140us/token, 4bit_kv_split: 190us/token
kv_cache_lookup: 12us/token (cold) -> 2us/token (hot)
cuda memcpy: 8us/token
overhead (dispatch+routing): 10us/token
fallback_count (4bit->fp32): 18
```

Priya: interesting — what calibration setup did you use? were you running dynamic or static per-layer calibration?

Alex: static per-layer calibrate with the pilot tool: `./calibrate --model redwood-v1 --quant 4 --batch 256 --calib-samples 2048`

Alex: calibration histograms looked fine but noticed a long tail in activation clipping for attn.qkv on layer 22. saved snippet: `layer22_q_clip=0.021 (p99)`

Sam: could be kernel selection heuristic. if the runtime sees high activation variance it prefers split-kernel paths -> more memcpy + kernel launches. that matches the higher memcpy/overhead numbers.

Jordan: also check batching heuristics. when sequences in the batch are uneven (mix of 128 + 1024) the runtime schedules multiple sub-batches and sometimes picks FP32 slow path for the larger sub-batch. saw this before in canary 2026-01.

Kai: re observability: we need per-token per-kernel counters surfaced in the console. currently our traces only show total tokens + avg latency. add metrics: kernel_selected{kernel_name}, kernel_exec_us, memcpy_us, kv_hit(boolean) at token granularity (aggregated histograms).

perf-bot: [alert] perf-regression-detect triggered for model=redwood-v1 quant=4bit on dedicated-a100 region-us-west2. delta=+22% per-token latency vs baseline-2026-01-30. CI run: 2026-02-18T09:15Z.

Priya: +1 on kernel_selected metric. also include calib_version tag so we can correlate poor calibrations. e.g. calib=static-2048-v2

Alex: quick experiment notes: reduced the batch mixing by grouping sequences by length before batching -> 4-bit perf improved to within 6% of FP8. suggests batching heuristic is a big factor.

Sam: actionables i can pick up:
- add kernel_selected counter to per-token telemetry (in proxy)
- add kv_hit tag to token spans
- instrument memcpy and kernel launch latencies as separate metrics

Jordan: I'll add a short eval harness to replay representative mixed-length workloads and run the calibration variants (static/dynamic) automatically. link to PR when ready.

Kai: for dashboard: new panels: per-model per-quant kernel_breakdown (p50/p95/p99), kv_hit_rate, fallback_rate, calib_tag filter. Also surface top layers by activation-clip p99.

Alex: for trace reference, sample trace snippet: ```
TRACE tokens: 1..8
- token 1: dispatch=3us, kv_lookup=2us, kernel=int8_kv_fused exec=158us, memcpy=7us
- token 5 (cold): dispatch=11us, kv_lookup=12us, kernel=4bit_kv_split exec=210us, memcpy=22us, fallback->fp32 (logged)
```

Priya: can someone open an issue with the perf bot? include the profiling dump + calibration artifacts + batching config I used. I'll attach calib histograms.

perf-bot: created issue #3241: "4-bit perf regression on a100 with mixed-length batches" by Alex. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/3241

Alex: thanks — will follow up with a minimal repro. for immediate mitigation, enable grouping-by-length for serving route `redwood-v1-4bit` and set fallback_threshold=0.12.

Kai: noted. i'll add the dashboard tiles and a runtime flag to enable grouping-by-length for a route.

Jordan: TL;DR: root cause = combination of calibration tail + batching mixing triggering split-kernel path + higher memcpy/launch overhead for 4-bit split kernels.

Sam: yep. prioritize telemetry first so we can catch similar regressions early.

Alex: :thumbsup:
